items.title: A coordinate event separates the two Gaussian targets

source.anchor: S2 targets/randomized algorithms/TV; Section3.3 zero-query case S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1 and S3.Ex3
source.attribution: On Complexity of Gaussian Sampling, arXiv2610.20492v1.
source.scope: Extracted signed Gaussian event-gap auxiliary and genuine PRIVATE arbitrary-common-probability-law TV obstruction. Not the zero-query algorithm model, T>=1/Q_G or complete Theorem3.1.

items.statement: The first-coordinate interval has probability larger by more than one eighth under the precision diag(kappa,1,...,1) target than under the identity-precision target. \pi_1(B)-\pi_0(B)>\frac18,\qquad B=\{x:|x_0|\le\tfrac12\},\quad\pi_j=N(0,A_j^{-1}). \(d\in\mathbb N,\ d\ge1\) and \(\kappa\in\mathbb R,\ \kappa\ge4\), including both endpoints. No upper bound on \(\kappa\) or extra block-dimension restriction is imposed. \(A_0=I_d\) and \(A_1=\operatorname{diag}(\kappa,1,\ldots,1)\) are precisions; their actual matrix inverses are the covariance parameters. Positivity and the inverse entries are derived inside the proof. \(x_0\) is the first Euclidean coordinate, indexed by0 in Lean and1 in the paper. The event uses the closed interval endpoint \(1/2\).
assumptions: \(d\in\mathbb N,\ d\ge1\) and \(\kappa\in\mathbb R,\ \kappa\ge4\), including both endpoints. No upper bound on \(\kappa\) or extra block-dimension restriction is imposed.

\(A_0=I_d\) and \(A_1=\operatorname{diag}(\kappa,1,\ldots,1)\) are precisions; their actual matrix inverses are the covariance parameters. Positivity and the inverse entries are derived inside the proof.
\(x_0\) is the first Euclidean coordinate, indexed by0 in Lean and1 in the paper. The event uses the closed interval endpoint \(1/2\).

obligations.label: Actual signed coordinate-event mass difference greater than1/8 for the two inverse-precision Gaussian targets.

bindings.boundary: This is the actual two-Gaussian event gap and its private arbitrary-common-probability-law TV obstruction. The Borel seed/stopping/output model, actual zero-query common-law and precision-class adapters, T>=1/Q_G and complete main lower bounds remain separate. These two inputs have different spectra, so this argument does not establish a disclosed-spectrum or fixed-eigenbasis result. No adaptive/Haar law, positive query-cap or expected-cost comparison, finite-precision oracle, shared integration, rendered desktop/mobile delivery, publication, purification/Exposition Seal or whole-Goal completion is claimed.

assumption_deltas.reason: The direction comes from the actual Gaussian variance/event calculation, not a converse inference from a TV lower bound.
